utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Elderkin. Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Bourgon, and Mr. Haynes. Any preliminaries? No. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, we are, as you can well see, sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Judge Stole hopefully will be with us tomorrow. There are no protective measures here, Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. No, no protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And on behalf of the Trial Chamber and Tribunal, I welcome you. You have been summoned as a witness by the Prosecution. Before you start your testimony, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. The text is going to be handed to you now by madam usher. Please read it aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. You're going to be asked a series of questions by Mr. Elderkin for the Prosecution who will then be followed on cross-examination by others. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm sure you all know that this witness is pursuant to Rule 92 ter, so it should be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. We met this morning, and you know I'm Rupert Elderkin, and I'll be asking you questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Did you make a statement to ICTY investigators on the 17th of March last year?

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And have you read the statement in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Do you attest that the statement accurately reflects what you said and that your answers would be the same if you were asked the same questions again today?

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would offer that statement into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 ter as P04438.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? We hear none, so let's proceed. The statement is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I should also ask the witness to state his name on the record. We haven't had that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: So, could you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: Nikodin Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And if I may read a brief summary of the statement into the record. The witness Nikodin Jovicic became a deputy commander of the uniformed police in Han Pijesak police station in May 1992. He was still in this post in July 1995. At that time, the commander of the uniformed police in Han Pijesak was Milan Perovic. The chief of the Han Pijesak police station was Goran Kanostrevac, nicknamed Kane. Before the war, the witness knew a person named Himzo Mujic, a labourer who was born between 1960 and 1965 and came from the village of Rijeka. This was a Muslim village a few kilometres towards Zepa. Mujic was one of the witness's operational contacts in his work as a policeman. The witness used to obtain information from Mujic regarding events in the Han Pijesak area. They lost contact in mid-1992. The witness heard that Himzo Mujic and his brothers went to Srebrenica and that his older brother Abdulah was killed in Srebrenica in 1992. He heard that the remaining brothers were killed after the fall of Srebrenica. The witness does not recall whether he had information about Mujic's whereabouts in July of 1995 or whether he tried to help Mujic, although he does not exclude that he might have done so. In any event, he was not in a position to help Mujic. The witness read an intercept from July 1995 bearing the ERN number 0080-1169 through 0080-1174, which is 65 ter 1323A. In this document, the name of Himzo Mujic is mentioned in the context that he would like to talk to Jovicic because he used to work for him. The witness believes that this intercept refers to Mujic wishing to talk to the witness, bearing in mind that Himzo Mujic cooperated with the witness before the war. The witness noticed the name of Neso Rubez in this intercept. He knew Nenad Rubez from elementary school in Han Pijesak and knew that Rubez had graduated from the law faculty. In 1995, Rubez was in the army doing office work, and the witness saw him in uniform in Han Pijesak. The witness does not recall any conversation with Rubez regarding Himzo Mujic, nor does he recall any conversation regarding Himzo Mujic with his then Chief Goran Kanostrevac. The witness heard that there was a military prison in Vlasenica known as Susica, but he does not recall the time-period. He never went there and had no contacts with prison warders. Your Honours, that's the end of the summary. I'd ask if I may show the intercept to the witness and ask him one question on that, and that will be the extent of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 1323A and its English translation, 1323B, in e-court. I also have the original of the intercept in this notebook if I may let the witness see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, is this the intercept you were shown in your interview with the investigators in 2008? It starts on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. That's all I have to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Elderkin. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jovicic. I have just one question for you with regard to your evidence so far. You've noticed in the notebook that you have just been shown the two extension numbers, and I know that a lot of time has lapsed, and my question to you is this: Do you remember these extensions 343 and 342? Did you ever call them? Did you use them? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: NIKODIN JOVICIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was quick. Any questions, Judge Kwon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I don't have any questions either, which means that you have probably established the record, at least in this trial. We're finished with your testimony, sir. Our staff will assist you in the arrangements necessary for your repatriation. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish to thank you for having come over, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Apart from -- Mr. Elderkin, you have -- apart from the statement, the 92 ter statement, you don't have any other documents, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: The intercept as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And that's listed as 1323A, and in fact there are printed versions as well. It's A through F on the tender list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose the other Defence teams are not that much interested? Okay. So the two documents are admitted. One has already been. Anything else? Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I owe you information about the two documents that concern -- 3D555 is going to be withdrawn from the list. This is Krstic. 3D556, by controlling the transcript we have established that not the whole text has been read out. What has been read out is not relevant [as interpreted], and that's why we adhere by our proposal that the evidence by Hadzihasanovic should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I just want to make sure that we've got the numbers correct. I remember them from yesterday. They are correct. So the only remaining one is 3D556.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I think our position remains the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because my question to you, I need to have it clear in my mind, is the following: You asked questions to that particular witness based on the Hadzihasanovic statement or document, anyway. What you are saying is the part read out and which shows up in the transcript is not really relevant while the rest is; is this what you are submitting?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I may have not been clear. Everything is relevant. What has been read out is also relevant. However, in order to gain a complete capture, it is about the strength of the 28th Division that Mr. Hadzihasanovic describes, and only one part in the description of the whole unit is contained in the part that was read out from the transcript. However, the whole picture, the whole description of that unit can be found on the previous page. That's why we believe that the Trial Chamber would benefit from having both pages in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the first conclusion is that the transcript as it appears on page 7, line 7, is not correct because what we have here is what has been read out is not relevant. So that needs to be corrected. The second thing is the following: Was the part that was not read out put to the witness or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not fully, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And on what basis, therefore, are you requesting its admission? Definitely, we cannot look at it or consider it as the testimony of Hadzihasanovic because he was not a witness yet. If it was not put to the witness -- I don't know what -- the Prosecution's position I think was clear yesterday, but -- it was clear enough, but my question is this. Ex admisus you did not put that part which you haven't read out during the testimony to the witness. On what basis are you seeking the admission of that part; and if admitted, what would it serve as a piece of evidence? What's its purpose, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole part concerns one and the same topic, the armament and the strength of the 28th Division, both pages. The part that was read out was provided to the witness in detail, and the context and the part that was not read is identical to the part that was read. They are both relevant parts. However, to avoid reading the entire text, we decided on reading just one part that refers to the entire context, and it is about the strength and the armament of the 28th Division. I don't know if I've been of assistance to you with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. It's now clearer. Only problem that I have, again, is if they are the same, if they say the same thing, why do you seek to have them both? I don't understand that. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Our objection is principally based on the precedent of something like this coming in. We'll take another look at is it, as well, to see if it's a fair description of the column and in which case we can agree that it'll come in. I just, as you know, take precedent of the situation and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's very fair on your part. So try to do that, and the moment you reach a decision, could you kindly communicate it to the Trial Chamber. Now, I need to consult my colleagues on something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we were checking actually when the dead-line is for the filing of the Defence responses to the Prosecution's motion for rebuttal evidence, and we have a confirmation that it falls this coming Monday. So please, if you can even file it before, that would be even better because we are not sitting on Friday, and it would give us the opportunity to work on it over the weekend as we do most of the time, much to our own detriment, but I think this is something that we need to chase up and decide as quickly as possible. So the earlier you file it, the better it will be. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I had said in an e-mail at some point to everyone that we can be ready to go the following Monday from that due date. Of course, we need your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, obviously. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can set up for the following Monday, and, in fact, we'll plan on setting up for the following Monday if you think you can get the decision out that week. If not, we'll take whatever you say, and we'll, of course, adjust based on your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing, Mr. McCloskey, as you can well imagine, you and all your colleagues on the other side, we have not started discussing the merits or the substance of your motion, reason being we don't know what the position of the various Defence teams will be, and we want to know -- want to hear the position of the Defence teams before we start our discussions. Our plan is to decide as quickly as possible after having the Defence teams' position. So I'm pretty sure that you can expect a decision sometime in the course of next week, as early as possible after the filing of the various responses. In the meantime, what we have prepared is the jurisprudence with which we were already quite familiar in any case, but that doesn't help us much until we've heard the Defences' position. Yes, we will also hand down soon - although I would prefer to deal with it orally - the decision on the various documents that were discussed yesterday. We'll try to come back to you either tomorrow, Thursday, if we can, on at least some of them, or then Monday. We'll see. You have got no other witnesses for today? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. On this topic, as you are aware, there's one outstanding witness that the order is following around somewhere and has yet to meet as far as I know, but we'll keep you updated on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And Mr. Sarapa, do you have -- what are your plans?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for today, we don't have a witness. Our expert witness, the linguistic expert will come tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That being so, we've got nothing else to do in here today. We stand adjourned, hoping that Judge Stole will be with us tomorrow; otherwise, we won't be able to sit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of March, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.01 a.m.,
